newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, seen firm despite Tudjman.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, seen firm despite Tudjman.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Tuesday and traders expect the bourse to firm despite concerns over the health of President Franjo Tudjman.
"We were all pleasantly surprised that the news about the president did not influence the capital market," Marijan Palic of Auctor brokerage said.
"There have been no shake-ups so far and I don't expect them in the following days either," he said.
Last week President Tudjman was admitted to a hospital in Washington where he is reported to be treated for stomach cancer.
Four of the 10 traded issues fell, three rose and three remained unchanged. Volume was lower at 15,914 shares and turnover fell to 15.5 million kuna from Friday's 20.1 million kuna.
Among the losers was foodprocessor Podravka, down seven kuna to 225 kuna on volume of 2,640 units. Palic said it was one of the best buys.
"Podravka is now one of the best investments, because it won't sink any further and it is only a matter of time before it rises," he said.
"I also expect a slight rise in Zagrebacka Banka because trading volume is growing," Palic added.
Zagrebacka, up six kuna to 1,006 kuna, was the most active stock with 10,588 ordinary shares traded.
The other fully-listed drugs firm, Pliva, eased 0.72 percent to 13,502.10 kuna on a volume of 264 shares.
